title: Set the singles sticks for singles: centres 3 ft (0.914 m) outside the singles court
instruction: This doubles court is hosting a singles match next, and the net is a doubles net (the dark band across the court marks where it hangs). The court is painted at 1:15 scale with the standard ITF lines. Put the two singles sticks in on the net line, one on each side of the court, standing upright where the rules put them, then let go.
context: Chair umpires, referees and court crews (O*NET 27-2023.00, sports officials) set and check a court before every match. Most club and tournament courts are combined doubles and singles courts with a doubles net. For a singles match the ITF Rules of Tennis (Rule 1) have the net held up at 1.07 m by two singles sticks whose centres are 0.914 m (3 ft) outside the singles court on each side, and the umpire checks them before play: sticks set anywhere else change the net's height over the singles court near the sidelines. Nothing on the court marks the spot. It has to be known (3 ft past the singles sideline, two thirds of the way across the alley) and measured from the lines; the usual mistakes are a stick on the singles sideline, in the middle of the alley or against the doubles sideline. At 1:15, 0.914 m is 61 mm, so each stick goes 33.5 cm from the centre line. Each arm sets the stick on its own side.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. The middle of a tennis court painted for doubles at 1:15: the 15 cm (2.25 m) of it either side of the net. Everything except the two sticks is fixed to the table. (1) Court surface: flat painted vinyl mats 1 mm thick glued to the table, their tops flush (the court surface, 1 mm above the table), x 20.0 to 50.0 cm: blue on the doubles court (|y| up to 36.57 cm), green outside it out to |y| 45.0 cm. (2) Net band: a dark grey vinyl strip flush with the court, 10 mm wide (x 34.5 to 35.5 cm, centred on the net line, x 35.0 cm), from y -42.7 to +42.7 cm; it marks where the doubles net hangs (the net is not modelled). (3) Lines: white vinyl strips 3 mm wide and 0.4 mm thick on the blue court, along x from x 20.0 cm to the net band and from the band to x 50.0 cm: the centre service line centred on y 0; the two singles sidelines, outer edges at y +27.43 and -27.43 cm (8.23 m apart at scale); the two doubles sidelines, outer edges at y +36.57 and -36.57 cm (10.97 m apart). (4) Two net posts: dark green painted wooden cylinders 25 mm across and 71 mm tall (1.07 m at scale) standing on the net line centred at x 35.0 cm, y +42.66 and -42.66 cm (0.914 m outside the doubles court). (5) Two singles sticks, alike: loose white ABS rigid bodies of 40 g each (uniform density), a 20 x 20 mm square post 63 mm tall on a 40 x 40 x 8 mm square foot, 71 mm tall in all, standing upright on the near court with their sides along x and y, centred at x 24.0 cm, y +15.0 cm and at x 24.0 cm, y -15.0 cm. Nothing else is on the table. A stick's centre is the middle of its foot's underside, where the post's axis meets the court; distances across the court are measured from the centre line to the outside edges of the lines, as court measurements are.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from both sticks' poses and both grippers (each pad-tip point, midway between the finger tips, and how far it is open), as a tape along the net line reads it. A stick is set when it is let go (no gripper's pad-tip point is less than 10 mm above the stick's top while within that gripper's finger reach of its axis: 94 mm fully open, 62 mm closed on the post, over every yaw), still (the middle of its post's axis, 35.5 mm up, moved under 1.5 mm along its path in each of the last two 0.5 s windows: under 3 mm over 1 s), upright (its post's axis within 10 degrees of vertical, foot down), standing on the court (its lowest point within 3 mm of the court surface: not on the other stick, on a post or held up) and on the net line (its centre within 6 mm of x 35.0 cm). A set stick earns 0.5 if its centre is within 8 mm of the ITF point, 0.914 m (3 ft) outside the singles court at 1:15: |y| = 33.53 cm, two thirds of the way across the alley; 0.25 if |y| is 27.0 to 37.0 cm (in its alley, a stick on either sideline included) but not at the ITF point; else 0. A stick that is not set earns 0. Each side of the court (y > 0, y < 0) scores the best of the sticks on it, so at most one stick counts per side. Score = the two sides' sum: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0. Every outcome: both sticks at their ITF points 1.0; one at its ITF point and the other in the middle of its alley (|y| 32.0 cm), on its singles sideline (27.3) or against its doubles sideline (36.6) 0.75; both on the singles sidelines, both mid-alley or both against the doubles sidelines 0.5; one at its ITF point and the other left at the start, still gripped, tipped over, upside down, stacked, off the net line or beside the net post (|y| over 37.0 cm) 0.5; both sticks in one alley, one at its ITF point, 0.5; one in its alley off the ITF point and the other not set 0.25; both left at the start, beside the posts, off the net line, tipped or still gripped 0. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 2 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Only the middle of the court is painted (1:15) and the net is not modelled: a painted band marks where it hangs, so the sticks stand on its line instead of propping a net cord. The sticks are 20 mm square posts (0.30 m at scale; the ITF limit is 7.5 cm) on an added foot so they can be gripped and stand alone; the net posts are over-scale. The line positions and the 3 ft offset are scaled exactly. The grippers are read only to check that each stick was let go.
reset_notes: Stand the two singles sticks back upright on the near court, sides along x and y, centred at x 24.0 cm, y +15.0 cm and at x 24.0 cm, y -15.0 cm. The court mats, lines and net posts are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
